title.narrative: Rapid Funding for Lifesaving Protection Services for Returnees from Sudan in Aweil East and North

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to provide critical protection assistance and services to South Sudanese returnees in Aweil East and North, focusing on child protection and gender-based violence (GBV). The project seeks to enhance the safety, dignity, and well-being of returnees by addressing specific needs and building local capacity to respond effectively to protection issues. The target groups, South Sudanese returnees, face significant vulnerabilities due to the ongoing conflict in Sudan. Children are particularly at risk of exploitation, abuse, and neglect. Women and girls are at heightened risk of sexual violence and exploitation, especially in overcrowded transit centers. There is a critical shortage of facilities and trained personnel to provide necessary support and a lack of awareness among returnees about available protection services.ltbrgtThe project aligns with the South Sudan Protection Cluster Strategy Response plans for 2025, addressing Strategic Objective 1: "Vulnerable crises-affected people have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable, safe, and dignified access to life-saving assistance to meet their needs." Key activities include identification and referral of child protection concerns, GBV risk monitoring and mitigation, awareness campaigns, specialized case management, family tracing and reunification, cash and voucher assistance, distribution of dignity kits, and staff training. The project emphasizes the involvement of local actors, capacity-building for local staff, use of local resources, and mechanisms for community feedback and participation. This ensures cultural appropriateness, sustainability, and responsiveness to the needs of the affected populations.ltbrgtThe project integrates protection principles across various sectors, focusing on child protection, GBV, cash distribution, and staff training. This holistic approach ensures that humanitarian aid targets the most vulnerable, enhances safety and dignity, and promotes human rights. The project actively involves crisis-affected people in design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation processes. Community consultations, feedback mechanisms, and participatory evaluation methods ensure that the project remains responsive and relevant to their needs. Confidential reporting channels for Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) complaints are established, ensuring accessibility and confidentiality. Regular reviews and follow-up procedures ensure timely responses and necessary referrals.ltbrgtThe project integrates gender-responsive policies and activities, promoting the empowerment of women and girls. Community consultations and focus group discussions ensure their needs and priorities are reflected in the project design. The project addresses barriers faced by persons with disabilities through community consultations, accessibility audits, and collaboration with disability-focused organizations. Inclusive safety protocols and training programs ensure their protection and participation. The project collaborates with other stakeholders at sector/cluster and inter-sector/cluster levels to align efforts and avoid duplication. Regular communication and joint planning sessions ensure cohesive and integrated responses. This comprehensive approach aims to enhance the overall resilience and well-being of returnees, ensuring their safety, dignity, and well-being.ltbrgtlt/pgt
